description:
The Council wishes to invite tenders for the supply of services in respect of general landscaping works throughout the District of Blaby, most of which will be within Parish or District Council owned Parks & Open Spaces (POS).\r
\r
Blaby District Council (the Council) has an ongoing programme of general landscaping works throughout the District. These works are funded from a number of budget areas and are generally ad hoc in nature. The Council therefore wishes to establish a framework agreement which allows it to procure these works in a more streamlined and cost effective way.\r
\r
All of the schemes will be located within the District of Blaby, most of which will be within Parish or District Council owned Parks & Open Spaces (POS).\r

title: Blaby District Council - Further Competition under ESPO RM6280 Postal Services and Solutions Lot 6 Hybrid Mail, Digital and Transformational Communications
description:
The Council invited further competition responses for the supply of goods and services in respect of Hybrid Mail Services for ALL outgoing mail (bulk and ad hoc) for Blaby District Council. 
The objectives of this contract are: 
The Council wishes to appoint a provider or providers to enter into a contract to assume overall responsibility for the production (printing and enclosing) and distribution (post) of all outgoing printed letters.  
Other key objectives include but are not limited to: 
Free up valuable staff from mailing activity. 
Minimise transportation costs incurred by the current mail delivery process by saving on fuel costs, handling costs and carbon emissions. 
Increased transparency and document integrity. 
Faster communications to the recipient in the quickest time possible. 
Eliminate/reduce investment on associated equipment costs. 
Improve efficiency of process. 
Improve security of mailing. 
Improve cost controls (incl. itemised billing with a breakdown to user or Business Unit level); 
Improve control over corporate image and branding. 
Blaby District Council wanted to collaborate with providers willing to accept change and eager to innovate new ways of communicating.

title: Short Breaks (Play & Leisure) and Domiciliary Care Services for Children with Disabilities Framework
description:
Leicestershire County Council is conducting a procurement to establish a Framework Agreement in accordance with the Light-Touch Regime requirements of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (SI 2015/102) (PCR 2015) for the purpose of procuring service providers to deliver services with regards to Short Breaks (Play & Leisure) and Domiciliary Care for Children with Disabilities.\r
\r
The requirement will be broken down into lots as described below.\r
\r
Lot 1 - Short Breaks (Play & Leisure): Short breaks provide opportunities for disabled children and young people to spend time away from their parents and carers, with friends and peers, for positive opportunities.  They are intended to promote their positive mental health and emotional well-being.  Short Breaks normally occur on a regular and planned basis and should be part of an integrated programme of support which is regularly reviewed.  Emergency Short Break provision will need to be provided from time to time.\r
\r
Lot 2 - Domiciliary Care\r
Domiciliary care is a statutory service that the Council has a duty to provide and it relates to the provision of care and support to children and families in their own home (e.g. personal care, meal preparation, moving and handling etc.).  The service can only be provided following an assessment of need and if certain thresholds are met. This service is not exclusively for disabled children and young people although they make up the vast majority of service users.  The framework covers two broad areas of domiciliary care - domestic tasks and sitting services.\r
\r
It is anticipated multiple Providers will be awarded on to each lot.\r
\r
It is intended that the Framework will commence on 01/04/2025 and that it will be in place for an initial period of one year ending 31/03/2026. There are three options to extend the framework in 12 month increments to a maximum end date of 31/03/2029.\r
\r
The Framework will be subject to review and re-opening. The Framework will be re-opened when the Council believes that reopening competition would be beneficial in terms of meeting demand and ensuring the framework is fit for purpose. This could be on an annual basis, to align with the framework's anniversary, and/or at any other time the Council deems necessary.\r

title: FEW1457 - Home Care Service, Leicester
description:
A procurement exercise for homecare services (ASC0307 - Home Care Services, Leicester) went live on 26th February 2024. The indicative timeline indicated that the contract award wouldn't take place until September/October 2024, which did not leave enough time to mobilise contracts, before the previous contracts were to expire on 6th October 2024. This is a statutory service, and a waiver was produced to bridge the gap between the previous contracts ending and the new arrangements being in place after a compliant procurement exercise.

The Authority received a high volume of bids for the ASC0307 - Home Care Services procurement exercise and to allow for the Authority to appropriately evaluate the high volume of tenders received, a new waiver has been put forward to continue the delivery of existing arrangements and allow additional time for the current procurement process. This will then enable the Authority to bridge the gap between existing arrangements ending and new homecare services commencing.

title: FEW1333 - Home Care Services Leicester
description:
The current Home Care Framework (currently named the Domiciliary Support Service) is due to expire on 6th October 2024 with procurement planned for October/November 2023. The contract had the option to extend for up to two years, and these have been utilised. The current jointly commissioned Framework began on 9th October 2017 and is supported by the Leicester, Leicestershire and Rutland NHS Integrated Care Board. A commissioning review has been undertaken to re-procure this statutory provision. A multi-disciplinary programme board has overseen the review arrangements which are led by senior officers in the ASC strategic commissioning team. Members include representatives from the Integrated Care Board and NHS Midlands & Lancashire Commissioning Support Unit.

The tender opportunity for the provision of ASC0288 - Home Care Service was advertised on 15th November 2023. The deadline for submissions was 2pm on Tuesday 19th December 2023. In February 2024, due to reasons beyond the Council's control and in line with section 4.22.10 of the ITT (Part One) document, the decision was made to abort the current procurement process ASC0288 - Home Care Service Leicester. A final award will therefore not be made, and the procurement process has been terminated. 

A new procurement exercise for homecare services went live on 26th February 2024. The indicative timeline indicates that contract award won't take place until September/October 2024, which does not leave enough time to mobilise contracts, before the existing contracts expire on 6th October 2024. This is a statutory service, and the waiver is required to bridge the gap between the current contracts ending and the new arrangements being in place after a compliant procurement exercise.
